# Just enough dplyr {#sec-dplyr}

Nearly every plot in this course needs the data summarised, filtered, or
reshaped before it can be drawn.

That work isn't ggplot2, and I don't teach it in the room. But you can't do any
of this on your own data without it, so here's the short version. Four verbs and
one reshape, which is all the course actually uses.

::: {.overview}

## Overview {.unnumbered}

**Duration** 10 minutes, optional

**Questions**

<!-- These map onto the sections below, in order. If you move a section, move its question. -->

- How do I keep only the rows I want?
- How do I make a new column?
- How do I go from 37,700 rows to one per hour?
- How do I get my data into the shape ggplot2 wants?

:::

## `filter()`

<!-- Keeping rows. One sensor, one month.

     Use the exact filters the chapters use, so this doubles as a reference for
     the code they have already run:
       filter(sensor_name == "Flagstaff Station")      @sec-computed
       filter(hour == 8)                               @sec-computed
       filter(sensor_name %in% c(...))                 @sec-computed
     == for one, %in% for several, and the classic gotcha of = instead of ==. -->

## `mutate()` and `if_else()`

<!-- Making columns. day_type from week_day is the one the course leans on
     hardest, in @sec-comparing.

       mutate(day_type = if_else(week_day %in% c("Saturday","Sunday"),
                                 "weekend", "weekday"))

     This exact line appears in @sec-computed and again in @sec-comparing, so
     it earns its own worked explanation here: test, value if true, value if
     false. Mention case_when() for more than two outcomes and leave it. -->

## `group_by()` and `summarise()`

<!-- The one that matters. Mean count per hour per sensor is the shape behind
     almost every plot in @sec-comparing onwards.

     37,700 rows in, 24 rows out. Show the row count shrinking - that is the
     whole concept and a dimension printout makes it concrete.

     Two things that bite, both of which they will hit:
       - na.rm = TRUE. 2,548 missing hours, so without it every mean is NA.
         Already flagged as a Your Turn in @sec-computed.
       - the grouping persists. summarise() peels one layer, which is why the
         chapters call ungroup(). Show it rather than just saying it.

     count() belongs here too, as the shorthand that @sec-computed uses to
     explain geom_bar(). -->
